chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Musawi narrated to me from Ubaydullah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is an obligation on the wealthy to visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) twice a year, and it is an obligation on the poor to visit it once a year.

key_terms.الْغَنِيِّ: The wealthy / those with financial means
key_terms.الْفَقِيرِ: The poor / those with limited means
key_terms.حَقٌّ: Obligation / right (in this context, a religious duty)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of times one must visit the grave of Imam Husayn annually according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a jurisprudential baseline for the frequency of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine, linking spiritual obligation to economic capacity. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of balancing devotional duties with practical livelihood, ensuring that the poor are not burdened while the wealthy are encouraged to maintain a deeper, more frequent connection to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Mūsawi narrated to me from ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Nahīk, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Abī Ayyūb (Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Uthmān), who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
It is an obligation on those who are wealthy to go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) twice a year and on those who are poor to go once a year.
